solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He searched frantically bringing bad luck!

indicators.note: doing something frantically means in a wild disordered way, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man rummaging in a panic brings misfortune on himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges HE SEARCHED; 'bringing' only links. HARD CHEESE is a British idiom for bad luck, often said with little sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a British expression meaning tough luck or misfortune, often said dismissively.

clue.text: Sweet smell, something annoying

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a bug is an irritation, something that bugs you

explanation.surface: A pleasant fragrance turns out to be irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British informal for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a striped boiled mint candy popular in Britain.

clue.text: Turner does this to art, shocking English

indicators.note: shocking, as in jolted out of place, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The painter Turner shocks English art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J.M.W. Turner but is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordplay definition: anything that turns spins round an axis.

clue.text: Chap to show impertinence in intimate dancing style

parts.note: a chap is a jaw or cheek
taken as written
cheek means impertinence

explanation.surface: A fellow cheekily breaking into a slow dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man but is the old word for jaw or cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: dancing close, faces touching, as in the Irving Berlin song.

clue.text: Repeat one before foxtrot

definitions.meaning: a repetition of sound bouncing back
the NATO phonetic code word for E comes just before F's code word

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dance: do it again, a single step before the foxtrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Double meaning: a reflected sound, and the radio alphabet word for E.

clue.text: What the Metrication Board wants to do for recycling facilities

definitions.text: What the Metrication Board wants to do
definitions.meaning: a body converting to metric would abolish imperial units of length
yards where scrap metal is collected and reused

explanation.surface: The metric authority's agenda includes junk yards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Metrication Board was the UK body that promoted metric units in the 1970s; read as two words the answer says what it wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: places that collect discarded metal for reuse.

clue.text: River goddess is doubled up

indicators.note: doubled up means the little word is written twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that a river deity is folded over.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is both the Egyptian goddess and the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford, so the definition covers both senses at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: the Egyptian goddess, and also the stretch of the Thames at Oxford.

clue.text: Sort of mushroom — member of Muslim group holds a thousand

indicators.note: holds means the believer's name contains the other letters

parts.note: a Shiite belongs to the Shia branch of Islam
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A Muslim believer carrying a thousand mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an edible East Asian fungus used in cooking.

clue.text: Hat — 'Ispanic fellow right in such

indicators.note: in puts the Spaniard and the letter for right inside the short word

parts.note: so means such, as in 'so great'
hombre is Spanish for man; dropping the H, as the clue's spelling does, gives ombre

explanation.surface: A hat, the sort a Hispanic man would wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''Ispanic' signals the dropped H of HOMBRE. The surface also hints at the hat's Mexican origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wide-brimmed Mexican headwear.

clue.text: Instrument blown after affair's high point

indicators.note: after places the instrument behind the word for affair

parts.note: an affair is a matter, as in 'a private matter'
a horn is a brass instrument that is blown

explanation.surface: Someone blows a horn once a love affair reaches its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests romance but means simply a matter or business. 'high point' is literal: the Swiss peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Alpine peak on the Swiss-Italian border, literally a lofty summit.

clue.text: Old Asian country is turning American

indicators.note: turning means the short word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: A former Asian nation is becoming Americanised.
explanation.definitionFit: History: the former name of Thailand, used until 1939.

clue.text: Like the Valkyries, second in one composition of Wagner after another

indicators.note: after places the other work behind the first piece
in places the short time inside the rearranged composer's name
a composition of the name means its letters made into a new arrangement

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
another composition of Wagner, his Ring cycle

explanation.surface: A puzzle about one Wagner work following another, like Die Walküre in the Ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition of' gives WARNGE; 'one ... after another' means the Ring, Wagner's other great work, follows the first composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the Valkyries are warlike battle maidens who choose the slain, so they relish combat.

clue.text: Mounted cop catching on

parts.note: mounted means up, as on horseback
to cop is slang for to catch or take

explanation.surface: A police officer on horseback is grabbing hold of a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted cop' reads as a horseback policeman, but 'cop' is the verb to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: understanding or comprehension, as in 'quick on the uptake'.

clue.text: Special dish to display prominently

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: A chef's special served on a fine dish to show it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to splash a story across a front page, giving it wide publicity.

clue.text: Like a rogue get annoyed about worries

indicators.note: about means going round, so the annoyance surrounds the worries

parts.note: to pique is to irritate; piqued means annoyed
cares are worries

explanation.surface: A rascal becomes irritated by his troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary term: describing fiction about a roguish wandering hero.

clue.text: Tourist in rank beset by wild blow

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the punch wraps round the word for rank

parts.note: a haymaker is a wild swinging punch
olid is a rare word meaning rank or foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A sightseer caught in a queue is hit by a sudden flailing punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a row or queue but means smelly, giving the rare word OLID. 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person on vacation, visiting places for pleasure.

clue.text: Clamber's put another way

indicators.note: put another way means the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: the word plus its S, used as letters

explanation.surface: A rewording of the verb for climbing awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: rearranged, CLAMBERS gives the answer, and the answer is another way of saying clamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to climb hastily using hands and feet.

clue.text: Overweight slob in cartoon — one's got to work out

parts.note: fat means overweight
Homer Simpson is the lazy father in The Simpsons

explanation.surface: A fat cartoon slob needs to get to the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' suggests exercise, but means figure out.
explanation.definitionFit: Agent noun: someone who fathoms things, i.e. who gets to the bottom of a problem.

clue.text: An emergency for Jumbo, say, caught taking risks by top of stairs

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
rash means acting recklessly, taking risks
a landing is the platform at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone caught being reckless near the head of a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' is a jumbo jet, not an elephant; 'by' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a forced, uncontrolled descent an aircraft such as a jumbo jet might have to make.

clue.text: Fierce woman teacher restricting students' time for frivolity

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the tutor surrounds the student event

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
rag week is a British students' charity festival of pranks

explanation.surface: A stern female lecturer cracks down on student fun.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG is a British university charity week of stunts and fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: a formidable, overbearing woman.

clue.text: Fix: something taken regularly

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a wire clip
a basic food or item in regular use

explanation.surface: A dose: the thing consumed on a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Double meaning: a wire fastener, and a basic regular commodity.

clue.text: A Greek character always one to succeed

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A Greek person who is forever destined to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who accomplishes goals and reaches success.

clue.text: Investigator to worry about the Queen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for worry goes round the royal letters

parts.note: to fret is to worry
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A detective is fretting over the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: someone who searches persistently, like the animal hunting out rabbits.

clue.text: Deceitful fellow upset bird

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, means turned over so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a liar is a deceitful person

explanation.surface: A dishonest man upsets a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a marsh-dwelling wading bird such as the water rail.

clue.text: Thousand in old money — a large sum

indicators.note: in places the letter for thousand inside the coin's name

parts.note: a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand in pre-decimal currency would be quite a lot of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOB was the slang name for a shilling in Britain's pre-1971 coinage. 'cost a bomb' means cost a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: British informal usage for a great deal of money.

clue.text: Adopting aggressive position settling account

definitions.meaning: taking a fighting stance, fists raised, ready to brawl
paying off what is owed, clearing a bill

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to fight while paying off a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrasal verb means both preparing to fight and paying what is owed.

clue.text: Work for long — take year off

indicators.note: off, with 'take', means the abbreviation for year is removed

parts.note: to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Labouring for ages: take a year away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... off' is the deletion signal split around 'year'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to gain money or reward through labour.

clue.text: New Conservative seen in scanty clothing not caring

indicators.note: seen in means the two letters appear inside the garment

parts.note: a negligee is a flimsy nightdress

explanation.surface: A new Tory politician spotted wearing skimpy clothes, without a care.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a careless lack of attention or concern; 'not caring' is read as a noun.
